title: Tool Interface Shape Registry and Heuristic Recovery Playbook
creator: Imani Brooks
description: Create a centralized 'shape registry' for function/tool JSON parameter definitions, plus a runtime heuristic recovery layer that maps common semi-structured inputs to expected shapes and produces human-friendly diagnostics. The goal is to reduce user-facing validation failures, provide clearer error messages, and capture telemetry for schema drift and common coercions.
background: We consistently see two classes of failures from tool/function calls: strict schema rejections caused by small shape mismatches (missing optional fields, wrong primitive type) and ambiguous errors that surface little context to the caller. Teams have built ad-hoc recovery layers in different runtimes. We need a unified registry and standard runtime heuristics that are versionable and observable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
proposal_summary: Introduce a registry service that stores canonical JSON parameter shapes with semantic metadata (required vs recommended, coercion hints, canonical examples). At runtime, validate incoming args against the registry, attempt deterministic and auditable heuristic repairs (e.g., string->number coercion, nesting unify, array wrapping), and return a standardized diagnostic object when recovery fails. Include feature flags for strict vs tolerant modes and telemetry hooks to capture repair rates and top-k failure patterns.
design_decisions: Keep registry entries flat JSON documents with a small set of metadata fields to ensure cross-language portability
Support a limited set of deterministic heuristics (coerce_scalar_types, unwrap_singleton_arrays, rename-known-aliases) rather than arbitrary user code
Expose both 'pre-validation repairs' (automatically applied) and 'suggested fixes' (returned in diagnostics) controlled by runtime flags
Record audit trail for each repair attempt: original payload, transformed payload, heuristic applied, and outcome (accepted/declined)
Version registry entries and include a compatibility map so older clients can be served with a fallback view
acceptance_criteria: Registry API implemented with CRUD for parameter shapes and versioning
Runtime validator integrated with serving runtime and able to call registry by model/tool binding
At least three deterministic heuristics implemented and gated behind flags
Diagnostics format documented and surfaced through Console error traces and SDK client exceptions
Telemetry: repair_rate, heuristic_breakdown, post-repair rejection_rate emitted to metrics backend
E2E tests covering: exact matches, repairable mismatches, unrecoverable mismatches, and opt-in strict mode
implementation_steps: Spec: define registry schema (id, version, description, json_schema, coercion_hints, examples, deprecation_notes)
Service: lightweight HTTP registry with auth and audit logs (CRUD + list + version endpoint)
Runtime: validator middleware that queries registry cache and applies heuristics (pluggable chain)
SDKs: client-side opt-in lenient mode that mirrors server heuristics for better dev UX
Console: new diagnostics panel showing original vs repaired payload and heuristic metadata
Telemetry: map events to existing metrics/trace names and add Grafana dashboard
testing_plan: Unit: shape matching and each heuristic behavior with property tests
Integration: inject invalid payloads across hosted/dedicated/private deployments and assert deterministic outcomes
Load: registry caching behavior under sustained QPS and cold-cache latency characterization
User-facing: sample prompts from customer incidents replayed to measure reduction in validation errors
Security: ensure registry access requires proper auth and audit trail retention meets compliance
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable registry and heuristics for internal teams and feature-flagged customers
Phase 2 (limited): enable pre-validation repairs for low-risk heuristics only (coerce_scalar_types, unwrap_singleton_arrays)
Phase 3 (broad): enable full heuristic suite and client SDK opt-in lenient mode; monitor repair_rate and post-repair rejections
Phase 4 (opt-out strict): provide per-customer strict mode that returns standardized diagnostics without repairs
monitoring_signals: repair_rate: percentage of incoming calls where a heuristic modified the payload
post_repair_rejection_rate: fraction of repaired payloads still rejected by downstream tool
top_failure_signatures: aggregated shapes that fail validation repeatedly
latency_p50/p95 for registry lookups (cold vs warm cache)
console_error_volume: count of diagnostic objects surfaced to console per hour

notes: Avoid adding heuristics that change semantics (e.g., merging unrelated fields) — only deterministic low-risk transformations
Consider future support for schema 'profiles' tuned to different SDK languages (strongly typed vs dynamic)
Keep diagnostics compact but actionable: include example corrected payload, heuristic name, and link to registry entry
